words.enDefinition: An array whose number of element positions stays fixed after it is created.

examples.en: The lab used a fixed-size array with seven positions for the days of the week.
examples.zh: 实验课用一个有七个位置的「定长数组」来存放一周的各天。

examples.en: We replaced the fixed-size array when the assignment started accepting more readings than it could hold.
examples.zh: 作业开始接收超过原容量的读数后，我们换掉了这个「定长数组」。

collocations: store scores in a fixed-size array

words.enDefinition: An array-backed collection that can increase its storage capacity as elements are added.

examples.en: Our dynamic array grew when the program added a sixth colour to the drawing palette.
examples.zh: 程序给绘图调色板增加第六种颜色时，「动态数组」扩大了容量。

examples.en: The tutor used a dynamic array because the number of readings was unknown before the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师用了「动态数组」，因为练习开始前无法确定读数有多少。

words.enDefinition: source notation that creates an array from the specified element expressions

examples.en: We wrote a JavaScript array literal containing three colours for the first drawing exercise.
examples.zh: 我们写了一个包含三种颜色的 JavaScript「数组字面量」，供第一次绘图练习使用。

examples.en: The sample used an empty array literal before the program started collecting new entries.
examples.zh: 示例先用了一个空的「数组字面量」，程序随后才开始收集新条目。

collocations: use an array literal for test data

words.enDefinition: A numbering convention in which the first element has index zero.

examples.en: Because Java uses zero-based indexing, the second reading was stored at index one in the example.
examples.zh: Java 采用「从零开始的索引」，所以例题中的第二个读数存放在索引一处。

examples.en: The diagram explained zero-based indexing by numbering the blank boxes from zero through four.
examples.zh: 图上给空格依次标了零到四，以说明「从零开始的索引」。

words.enDefinition: A numbering convention in which the first element has index one.

examples.en: The MATLAB example used one-based indexing, so index one referred to the first recorded value.
examples.zh: MATLAB 示例采用「从一开始的索引」，因此索引一指向第一个记录值。

examples.en: We checked the language's one-based indexing convention before changing the row access in our exercise.
examples.zh: 在修改练习里读取表格行的代码前，我们先核对了该语言「从一开始的索引」规则。

collocations: compare one-based indexing with zero-based indexing

words.enDefinition: A value stored at one of an array's indexed positions.

examples.en: The instructor traced how the first array element changed when the recorded reading was corrected.
examples.zh: 老师逐步说明读数更正后，第一个「数组元素」怎样变化。

examples.en: We inspected each array element to find the missing colour in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 我们逐一检查「数组元素」，寻找课堂例子中缺失的一种颜色。

words.enDefinition: The number used to identify an element's position in an array.

examples.en: We used the array index to select one photograph from the small set shown in class.
examples.zh: 我们用「数组索引」从课堂展示的那小组照片中选出一张。

examples.en: Our tutor wrote the array index above each value so everyone could follow the example.
examples.zh: 老师在每个值上方写出「数组索引」，方便大家看懂示例。

collocations: use an array index to select a value

words.enDefinition: The limits defining the lowest and highest valid positions for a collection.

examples.en: The exercise asked us to check index bounds before reading a square on the board.
examples.zh: 练习要求我们先核对「索引边界」，再读取棋盘上的格子。

examples.en: We wrote the index bounds beside the array so the final valid position was clear.
examples.zh: 我们把「索引边界」写在数组旁，标清最后一个有效位置。

words.enDefinition: A message or description indicating that an index does not identify an accessible position.

examples.en: The Python exercise reported an index out of range error when we read past the final item.
examples.zh: 我们尝试读取最后一项之后的位置时，Python 练习报告了「索引超出范围」错误。

examples.en: Our tutor traced the index out of range message to a row number beyond the table.
examples.zh: 老师查明，「索引超出范围」的提示是因为行号超过了表格范围。

collocations: an index out of range error
handle an index out of range condition

words.enDefinition: In languages that support it, using negative indexes to address positions relative to the end of a sequence.

examples.en: We used negative indexing in Python to read the last colour in the palette.
examples.zh: 我们用 Python 的「负索引」读取调色板中的最后一种颜色。

examples.en: The tutorial explained negative indexing by counting backwards from the final entry in the list.
examples.zh: 教程从列表的最后一项往前数，以说明「负索引」。

collocations: explain negative indexing with a list

words.enDefinition: the number of array positions as defined by the array's indexing rules, including empty positions where the language allows them

examples.en: We printed the array length before checking how many samples the exercise had stored.
examples.zh: 我们先输出「数组长度」，再核对练习中存了多少个样本。

examples.en: The last index in the Java example was one less than the array length.
examples.zh: 在 Java 示例中，最后一个索引比「数组长度」小一。

collocations: compare two values with the array length

words.enDefinition: the number of elements an array-backed collection can hold in the storage currently allocated

examples.en: The diagram showed an array capacity of eight even though only three spaces contained elements.
examples.zh: 图示的「数组容量」是八，虽然只有三个位置存有元素。

examples.en: We kept the same array capacity after removing the last entry from the practice collection.
examples.zh: 从练习集合中移除最后一项后，我们保持原有的「数组容量」。

words.enDefinition: The number of elements actually stored in a collection, regardless of its reserved capacity.

examples.en: The dynamic array had a logical size of four while its storage could hold eight values.
examples.zh: 动态数组的「逻辑大小」是四，而它的存储空间能容纳八个值。

examples.en: Our example updated the logical size immediately after appending a colour to the palette.
examples.zh: 例题在把一种颜色追加到调色板之后，立即更新了「逻辑大小」。

words.enDefinition: Space in an array-backed collection allocated for elements that are not currently stored.

examples.en: Adding two scores took up unused array capacity without requiring any additional storage allocation.
examples.zh: 增加两个分数占用了「数组剩余容量」，因此无需额外分配存储空间。

examples.en: Our tutor shaded the unused array capacity differently from positions that already contained real values.
examples.zh: 老师对「数组剩余容量」与已存有实际值的位置用了不同的底色。

collocations: add entries using unused array capacity

words.enDefinition: A layout in which a block of successive elements occupies adjacent memory locations.

examples.en: The diagram showed contiguous storage as one block, with each numeric element directly beside the next.
examples.zh: 图示把「连续存储」画成一个块，各数值元素都紧挨着下一个元素。

examples.en: Our tutor contrasted contiguous storage for array elements with separately allocated nodes in a linked list.
examples.zh: 老师把数组元素的「连续存储」同链表节点各自分配内存作了对比。

collocations: compare contiguous storage with linked nodes

words.enDefinition: An internal array that stores the elements of another collection, such as a resizable list.

examples.en: The list used a backing array to store the colours while exposing methods for editing them.
examples.zh: 这个列表用「底层数组」存放颜色，同时对外提供编辑这些颜色的方法。

examples.en: We drew a larger backing array when the next addition no longer fit in the old storage.
examples.zh: 下一项放不进原存储空间时，我们画了一个更大的「底层数组」。

collocations: copy elements to a new backing array

words.enDefinition: To replace a collection's internal array with one of a different capacity while retaining its stored elements.

examples.en: We had to resize the backing array before the collection could accept another reading.
examples.zh: 集合再接收一个读数之前，我们得先「调整底层数组大小」。

examples.en: The diagram showed why we copy existing colours when we resize the backing array.
examples.zh: 图中说明了为什么「调整底层数组大小」时要复制原有颜色。

collocations: resize the backing array when full
resize the backing array before appending
copy entries when you resize the backing array

words.enDefinition: To make storage available for future entries without adding any elements yet.

examples.en: The example used a library method to reserve capacity before any of the scores arrived.
examples.zh: 十个分数都还未传入时，示例先调用预留函数「预留容量」。

examples.en: We decided to reserve capacity for the readings while leaving the collection logically empty.
examples.zh: 我们选择为读数「预留容量」，同时在逻辑上保持集合为空。

collocations: reserve capacity without changing the size

words.enDefinition: To reduce unused storage in a resizable collection while keeping the elements it currently contains.

examples.en: The tutor showed how to trim excess capacity after the Java list stopped receiving new values.
examples.zh: 老师演示了 Java 列表不再接收新值后怎样「缩减多余容量」。

examples.en: We checked that the recorded grades stayed unchanged when the example chose to trim excess capacity.
examples.zh: 示例选择「缩减多余容量」时，我们核对了已记下的成绩是否保持原值。

collocations: trim excess capacity in an array-backed list
decide when to trim excess capacity

words.enDefinition: A selected portion of an array described by a range of indexes.

examples.en: We used an array slice to inspect the middle three readings without printing the whole collection.
examples.zh: 我们用「数组切片」查看中间三个读数，省去了输出整个集合。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which positions an array slice included when the starting index was two.
examples.zh: 老师问，起始索引为二时，一个「数组切片」包含哪些位置。

collocations: create an array slice from a range

words.enDefinition: The start and stop positions that define the range selected by a slice.

examples.en: We moved the slice bounds by one position to select the next group of sample readings.
examples.zh: 我们把「切片边界」移动一个位置，来选取下一组样本读数。

examples.en: The diagram labelled the slice bounds separately so the excluded endpoint was easy to identify.
examples.zh: 图中单独标出了「切片边界」，以便辨认不含在内的端点。

words.enDefinition: A slice whose range includes the start position and excludes the stop position.

examples.en: The example used a half-open slice beginning at index two and ending just before index five.
examples.zh: 示例使用了一个「半开区间切片」，从索引二开始，到索引五之前结束。

examples.en: We drew a half-open slice to show why the value at the stop index was excluded.
examples.zh: 我们画了一个「半开区间切片」，说明为什么不包含终止索引处的值。

collocations: take a half-open slice of an array

words.enDefinition: To add an element at a chosen position, moving later elements if the collection preserves their order.

examples.en: The tutor showed how to insert at an index while keeping the other colours in order.
examples.zh: 老师演示了怎样「在指定索引处插入」并保持其他颜色的顺序。

examples.en: We let the user insert at an index chosen from the valid positions on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们允许使用者从练习表中选一个有效位置，然后「在指定索引处插入」。

collocations: insert at an index in a list
insert at an index before the final element
check the position before you insert at an index

words.zhGloss: 移除指定索引处的元素
words.enDefinition: To remove the item occupying a specified position without choosing it by value.
acceptedZhAnswers: 移除指定索引处的元素

examples.en: Our exercise let us remove at an index even when two entries had the same value.
examples.zh: 即使两个条目的值相同，练习也能让我们「移除指定索引处的元素」。

examples.en: The tutor showed how to remove at an index and shift the later entries left.
examples.zh: 老师演示了怎样「移除指定索引处的元素」，再将后续条目左移。

collocations: remove at an index in a list
remove at an index instead of by value
check the position before you remove at an index

words.enDefinition: To replace the value stored at a position without inserting a new position.

examples.en: We needed to overwrite an element when the lab corrected a temperature already stored in the array.
examples.zh: 实验课要更正数组里已有的一个温度值时，我们需要「覆盖原有元素」。

examples.en: The program could overwrite an element without changing the number of entries in the working list.
examples.zh: 程序可以「覆盖原有元素」，同时保持工作列表的条目数不变。

collocations: overwrite an element in an array
overwrite an element at a specified index
overwrite an element without changing the length

words.enDefinition: To add an item after all the items already in a collection.

examples.en: We chose to append an element whenever the lab recorded another measurement during the experiment.
examples.zh: 实验中每记录一个新的测量值，我们就「在末尾追加元素」。

examples.en: Our program could append an element once the player entered another colour for the palette.
examples.zh: 玩家为调色板输入另一种颜色后，程序就能「在末尾追加元素」。

collocations: append an element to a list
append an element at the end
append an element when space remains

words.enDefinition: To add an item before the first item in a collection.

examples.en: The code needed to prepend an element so the heading would appear before the existing entries.
examples.zh: 代码需要「在开头添加元素」，这样标题就会出现在原有条目之前。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether it was easier to prepend an element using a list with links.
examples.zh: 老师问，用带链接的列表「在开头添加元素」是否更方便。

collocations: prepend an element to a list
prepend an element at the front
prepend an element before existing entries

words.enDefinition: To move a group of elements by one or more index positions within an ordered collection.

examples.en: The diagram showed how to shift elements right before placing a new value at index two.
examples.zh: 图中展示了在索引二放入新值之前如何向右「移动元素位置」。

examples.en: We had to shift elements left so the array would have no gap after the removal.
examples.zh: 删除之后，我们得向左「移动元素位置」，这样数组中间才不会留下空位。

collocations: shift elements one position to the right

words.enDefinition: An array whose elements are addressed with two indexes, often interpreted as row and column.

examples.en: The puzzle stored its board in a two-dimensional array with one position for each square.
examples.zh: 这个谜题把棋盘存成「二维数组」，每个格子对应一个位置。

examples.en: We used a two-dimensional array to record three temperatures for each day of the week.
examples.zh: 我们用「二维数组」记录一周中每天的三个温度值。

collocations: access a cell in a two-dimensional array
store a grid in a two-dimensional array

words.enDefinition: A storage or traversal order that places elements from each row together before moving to the next row.

examples.en: The C example stored its table in row-major order, with each row followed by the next.
examples.zh: C 示例按「行优先顺序」存储表格，一行紧接着下一行。

examples.en: Our drawing labelled the one-dimensional positions in row-major order before converting them back to grid coordinates.
examples.zh: 我们在图中按「行优先顺序」标出一维位置，再换回网格坐标。

collocations: traverse a grid in row-major order
convert an index to row-major order

words.enDefinition: An array of arrays whose inner arrays may have different lengths.

examples.en: The C# example used a jagged array because some teams had more scores than others.
examples.zh: C# 示例采用「不规则数组」，因为有些队录入的分数比其他队多。

examples.en: We measured each row of the jagged array separately before displaying the practice table.
examples.zh: 显示练习表之前，我们分别测量了「不规则数组」每行的长度。

collocations: store rows in a jagged array
use a jagged array for unequal row lengths

words.enDefinition: To turn a multi-dimensional array or nested array structure into a single sequence of elements.

examples.en: We had to flatten an array before comparing its values with the worksheet's single list.
examples.zh: 我们需要先「把数组展平」，再把里面的值与练习表的一个列表作比较。

examples.en: The exercise asked us to flatten an array row by row to keep its order predictable.
examples.zh: 练习要求我们按行「把数组展平」，以确保元素顺序可预期。

collocations: flatten an array row by row
flatten an array into one dimension
flatten an array before displaying the results

words.enDefinition: A list that contains one or more lists as elements.

examples.en: Our Python exercise stored the board in a nested list with one inner list per row.
examples.zh: Python 练习用「嵌套列表」存放棋盘，每行对应一个内层列表。

examples.en: The program printed the two inner groups of the nested list on different lines.
examples.zh: 程序把「嵌套列表」内部的两组元素打印在不同行上。

collocations: store rows in a nested list

words.enDefinition: Changing an existing collection directly instead of building a replacement collection.

examples.en: The operation performed an in-place modification, so both variables referring to the list saw the new value.
examples.zh: 操作进行了「原地修改」，所以引用该列表的两个变量都能看到新值。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the sorting method used in-place modification or returned a separate list.
examples.zh: 老师问，排序方法执行的是「原地修改」，还是返回单独的列表。

collocations: perform in-place modification on a list

words.enDefinition: a collection whose elements are stored in nodes linked in sequence

examples.en: The linked list stored pictures in display order even when their storage locations were different.
examples.zh: 「链表」按显示顺序组织图片，即使图片的存储位置各不相同。

examples.en: Our tutor drew a linked list to show how nodes could hold values and references.
examples.zh: 老师画了一个「链表」，展示节点怎样存放值和引用。

words.enDefinition: A linked list in which each ordinary node carries a link to its successor only.

examples.en: The singly linked list could move from the first colour to the second by following one link.
examples.zh: 这个「单向链表」沿一条链接就能从第一种颜色移到第二种。

examples.en: We used a singly linked list because the exercise only needed movement towards the end.
examples.zh: 我们用了「单向链表」，因为练习只需要向表尾方向遍历。

collocations: insert into a singly linked list

words.enDefinition: A linked list with links to both the previous and next nodes.

examples.en: The doubly linked list let students move through the sample photo collection in either direction.
examples.zh: 借助「双向链表」，学生可向两个方向查看示例照片集。

examples.en: Our tutor drew two arrows between neighbouring nodes in the example of a doubly linked list.
examples.zh: 老师画「双向链表」示例时，在相邻节点之间画了两个方向的箭头。

collocations: insert into a doubly linked list
walk a doubly linked list backwards

words.enDefinition: A linked list whose links lead from its last node back to its first.

examples.en: We used a circular linked list to cycle through the names in a classroom game.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂游戏中用「循环链表」循环读取姓名。

examples.en: The exercise stopped walking the circular linked list when it returned to the starting node.
examples.zh: 练习遍历「循环链表」时，回到起始节点便停止。

collocations: detect a return to the start of a circular linked list

words.enDefinition: A record in a linked list storing an element and one or more connecting links.

examples.en: The diagram showed one list node for each book in the small classroom collection.
examples.zh: 图中给课堂小图书集里的每本书画了一个「链表节点」。

examples.en: We inspected a list node to see both its stored colour and its link.
examples.zh: 我们查看一个「链表节点」，看到了它存的颜色和链接。

collocations: attach a list node to its successor

words.enDefinition: The first node in a linked list, excluding any separate sentinel used by the implementation.

examples.en: The head node held the first card in the sequence shown on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 「头节点」保存了练习表所示序列中的第一张卡片。

examples.en: We checked the head node after adding a new colour before the original first item.
examples.zh: 把新颜色加到原第一项之前后，我们查看了「头节点」。

words.enDefinition: The node at the end of a linked list, excluding any separate sentinel.

examples.en: The tail node held the last recipe in the practice list before we added another.
examples.zh: 添加新食谱之前，「尾节点」保存了练习列表的最后一个食谱。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked where the tail node would be after deleting the final entry.
examples.zh: 练习表问，删除最后一项后「尾节点」会在哪里。

words.enDefinition: A pointer or reference used to locate the start of a linked list.

examples.en: The head pointer changed when the new list node became the first element in our example.
examples.zh: 例题中的新链表节点成为第一项后，「头指针」发生了变化。

examples.en: Our diagram used an arrow from the head pointer to the start of the chain.
examples.zh: 图中画了一条从「头指针」指向链起点的箭头。

words.enDefinition: A pointer or reference to the end of a linked list.

examples.en: We kept a tail pointer so the example could find the last node without walking the list.
examples.zh: 我们保留了一个「尾指针」，让例题不必遍历链表就能找到最后一个节点。

examples.en: Our tutor changed the tail pointer after appending a new book to the practice list.
examples.zh: 在练习链表末尾加了一本书后，老师更新了「尾指针」。

words.enDefinition: A pointer or reference that identifies a node's immediate successor.

examples.en: The next pointer led from the blue node to the green node in our diagram.
examples.zh: 在我们的图中，「后继指针」从蓝色节点指向绿色节点。

examples.en: We changed the next pointer so the new node appeared between two existing colours.
examples.zh: 我们更新了「后继指针」，使新节点出现在两个原有颜色节点之间。

collocations: set the next pointer of a node

words.enDefinition: A pointer or reference that identifies a node's immediate predecessor.

examples.en: The previous pointer led towards the first node when students traced the sample list backwards.
examples.zh: 学生倒着追踪示例链表时，「前驱指针」指向靠近第一个节点的方向。

examples.en: We checked the previous pointer after inserting a card between two cards that were already linked.
examples.zh: 在已链接的两张卡片之间插入一张卡片后，我们核对了「前驱指针」。

collocations: update the previous pointer of the successor

words.enDefinition: The part of a node that stores a pointer or reference connecting it to another node.

examples.en: The link field was blank in the drawing until we connected the card to its neighbour.
examples.zh: 我们把卡片连到相邻卡片之前，图中的「链接字段」是空的。

examples.en: The worksheet separated the link field from the box holding the value of each node.
examples.zh: 练习表把「链接字段」与存放各节点值的方框分开画了。

collocations: inspect the link field in a node

words.enDefinition: The data carried by a node, apart from its structural links.

examples.en: We changed one node value without changing any of the arrows between the cards.
examples.zh: 我们改了一个「节点值」，卡片之间的箭头维持原样。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the node value with the number written on the separate answer sheet.
examples.zh: 老师把「节点值」与另一张答题纸上写的数字作了比较。

words.enDefinition: An extra node marking a position in a structure and carrying no ordinary collection element.

examples.en: The sentinel node simplified the example because every data node then had a predecessor.
examples.zh: 有了「哨兵节点」，每个数据节点都有前驱，使例题更简单。

examples.en: We drew a sentinel node in grey so nobody would count it as a stored score.
examples.zh: 我们把「哨兵节点」画成灰色，以免有人把它算作已存成绩。

collocations: use a sentinel node to handle an empty list
link a sentinel node to the first element

words.enDefinition: A link with no target, often marking the end of a non-circular linked list.

examples.en: The final box contained a null link because there was no node after the last colour.
examples.zh: 最后一种颜色之后已没有节点，所以最后一个方框里是「空链接」。

examples.en: We stopped when the diagram showed a null link where the next node would have been.
examples.zh: 图中原本应指向后继节点的地方是「空链接」，我们就停止了遍历。

collocations: use a null link at the tail

words.enDefinition: To add a new list node immediately after an existing one by changing the relevant links.

examples.en: The tutor showed how to insert after a node by updating the links in our drawing.
examples.zh: 老师通过更新图上的链接，演示怎样「在节点后插入」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked where the new colour would appear if we chose to insert after a node.
examples.zh: 练习表问，如果选择「在节点后插入」，新颜色会出现在哪里。

collocations: insert after a node in a list
insert after a node without shifting elements
prepare the link before you insert after a node

words.enDefinition: To remove a node from a linked structure by updating its neighbours or the list's endpoints.

examples.en: The class drew two new arrows to unlink a node from the middle of the list.
examples.zh: 为了让中间的「节点脱离链表」，全班画了两条新箭头。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what must change if we unlink a node that currently comes first.
examples.zh: 老师问，如果要「使节点脱离链表」，而它当前是第一个节点，必须改哪些内容。

collocations: unlink a node from a list
update neighbouring links to unlink a node
unlink a node before moving it

words.enDefinition: To take away the first data node and update where the linked list begins.

examples.en: We updated the starting reference before we could remove the head node in our sample.
examples.zh: 在例题中「移除头节点」之前，我们先更新了起始引用。

examples.en: The worksheet asked what remained if we chose to remove the head node from a one-item list.
examples.zh: 练习表问，如果从只有一项的链表中「移除头节点」，还会剩下什么。

collocations: remove the head node of a list
update the start when you remove the head node

words.enDefinition: To visit the nodes of a linked list in sequence by following their links.

examples.en: We needed to traverse a linked list to print the stored names in their recorded order.
examples.zh: 为了按记录顺序输出已存姓名，我们需要「遍历链表」。

examples.en: Our tutor showed how to traverse a linked list from its first node to its last.
examples.zh: 老师演示了怎样从第一个节点到最后一个节点「遍历链表」。

collocations: traverse a linked list from the head
traverse a linked list to read its values
traverse a linked list in reverse

words.enDefinition: To move from the current linked node to the node identified by its successor reference.

examples.en: We had to follow the next link before reading another colour from the sample chain.
examples.zh: 从示例节点链读取下一种颜色前，我们得「沿后继链接移动」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked us to follow the next link and write down the node we reached.
examples.zh: 老师让我们「沿后继链接移动」，并记下到达的节点。

collocations: follow the next link from the head
follow the next link to its target
follow the next link while traversing

words.enDefinition: A linked list with no data nodes, even if its implementation uses a sentinel.

examples.en: Our empty linked list contained only a sentinel, so the exercise reported a size of zero.
examples.zh: 我们的「空链表」只有一个哨兵节点，因此练习报告的大小为零。

examples.en: Before adding the first note, we checked how the diagram represented an empty linked list.
examples.zh: 加入第一条笔记之前，我们查看了图中怎样表示「空链表」。

collocations: test for an empty linked list
append to an empty linked list

words.enDefinition: A linked list containing exactly one ordinary node.

examples.en: In our single-node list, the same card was both the first and the last item.
examples.zh: 这个「单节点链表」里，同一张卡片既是第一项也是最后一项。

examples.en: The tutor used a single-node list to test what happened when the only item was removed.
examples.zh: 老师拿「单节点链表」测试删除唯一一项时会发生什么。

collocations: remove an item from a single-node list

words.enDefinition: To transfer existing nodes within or between linked lists by changing their connections.

examples.en: The classroom example showed how to splice a list into the middle of another list.
examples.zh: 课堂示例演示了怎样在另一个链表的中间「拼接链表节点」。

examples.en: We could splice a list of songs into the playlist without recreating any song entries.
examples.zh: 我们可以把一组歌曲的「链表节点拼接」到播放列表中，无需重新创建歌曲条目。

collocations: splice a list into another list
splice a list without copying its elements
decide where to splice a list

words.enDefinition: Visiting the elements of a structure in the reverse of its usual order.

examples.en: Backward traversal let the classroom playlist display its songs from the final entry to the first.
examples.zh: 课堂示例的播放列表通过「反向遍历」从最后一项到第一项依次显示歌曲。

examples.en: The tutor attached a predecessor link to each node before demonstrating backward traversal to the class.
examples.zh: 老师给每个节点加了前驱链接，然后向全班演示「反向遍历」。

collocations: start backward traversal at the end

words.enDefinition: To change the links among existing nodes without replacing their stored values.

examples.en: The diagram showed how to relink nodes after putting the picture cards in a different order.
examples.zh: 图中展示了把图片卡片换个顺序后如何「重新连接节点」。

examples.en: The worksheet showed how to relink nodes without changing the values inside any of them.
examples.zh: 练习表展示了怎样在保持各节点内原值的同时「重新连接节点」。

collocations: relink nodes in a different order
relink nodes without copying their values

words.enDefinition: To change the order of a linked list so it starts with its previous last element.

examples.en: Our diagram showed how the arrows changed when we chose to reverse a linked list.
examples.zh: 图中展示了选择「反转链表」后箭头怎样变化。

examples.en: The exercise asked what the first item would be after we used code to reverse a linked list.
examples.zh: 练习问，用代码「反转链表」之后，第一项会是什么。

collocations: reverse a linked list in place
reverse a linked list by updating links
test a function that can reverse a linked list

words.enDefinition: A structure with one accessible end where the most recently added item is removed first.

examples.en: The practice editor used a LIFO stack to keep the latest change available for undo.
examples.zh: 练习用的编辑器采用「后进先出栈」，便于优先撤销最近一次改动。

examples.en: We drew a LIFO stack with the newest card above all the cards added earlier.
examples.zh: 我们画了一个「后进先出栈」，最新加入的卡片位于所有早先卡片上方。

collocations: store items in a LIFO stack
remove the top item from a LIFO stack

words.enDefinition: Describing an order in which the item added most recently is the first removed.

examples.en: The stack followed last-in, first-out order, so the last colour added was removed first.
examples.zh: 这个栈遵循「后进先出」顺序，因此最后加入的颜色最先被取出。

examples.en: The teacher used the phrase last in, first out to describe the order of those cards.
examples.zh: 老师用「后进先出」来描述这些卡片的取出顺序。

words.enDefinition: The end of a stack where items are added, inspected, and removed.

examples.en: The last score we entered appeared at the top of the stack in the diagram.
examples.zh: 我们最后输入的分数显示在图中的「栈顶」。

examples.en: Our example checked the top of the stack before deciding whether to remove the card.
examples.zh: 例题先查看「栈顶」，再决定是否取出那张卡片。

collocations: read the top of the stack
add an item to the top of the stack
remove an item from the top of the stack

words.enDefinition: The end of a stack opposite the end used for insertion and removal.

examples.en: The first card remained at the bottom of the stack after two more were added.
examples.zh: 又放入两张卡片后，第一张仍留在「栈底」。

examples.en: We reached the bottom of the stack after taking out each later card in turn.
examples.zh: 我们依次取出后放入的每张卡片后到达「栈底」。

collocations: the item at the bottom of the stack
reach the bottom of the stack
remain at the bottom of the stack

words.enDefinition: To insert an item at the top of a stack.

examples.en: The tutor showed us which end to use when we push onto a stack.
examples.zh: 老师演示了「压入栈」的时候应该用哪一端。

examples.en: We compared what happens when we push onto a stack with adding to a queue.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「压入栈」与加入队列时分别会发生什么。

collocations: push onto a stack after reading an item
push onto a stack in order
keep track of what you push onto a stack

words.enDefinition: To remove the top item from a stack and usually return it.

examples.en: Each time we pop from a stack in the example, its top card is removed.
examples.zh: 在例题中每次「从栈中弹出」时，取出的都是栈顶卡片。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked which card would be removed first if we chose to pop from a stack.
examples.zh: 练习表问，如果选择「从栈中弹出」，最先被移除的是哪张卡片。

collocations: pop from a stack after checking it
decide when to pop from a stack

words.enDefinition: To inspect the top item of a stack without removing it.

examples.en: Our code could peek at the top before deciding whether to remove the latest colour.
examples.zh: 代码可以先「查看栈顶元素」，再决定是否移除最后加入的颜色。

examples.en: The exercise asked us to peek at the top and record the size before and after.
examples.zh: 练习让我们「查看栈顶元素」，并记录查看前后的栈大小。

collocations: peek at the top before removing an item
peek at the top of a stack
peek at the top without changing the stack

words.enDefinition: Trying to remove an item from a stack that contains no items.

examples.en: The practice stack reported stack underflow when we tried removing a card after taking the last one.
examples.zh: 我们取走最后一张卡片后又试着取卡，练习用的栈报告「栈下溢」。

examples.en: Our tutor added an empty check so the example could report stack underflow clearly.
examples.zh: 老师加了一个判空检查，让例题能清楚地报告「栈下溢」。

words.enDefinition: A stack that can hold at most a specified number of items.

examples.en: The bounded stack held at most three cards in the worksheet we used in class.
examples.zh: 课堂练习表里的「有界栈」最多只能放三张卡片。

examples.en: We tested what the bounded stack did after all its available positions were occupied.
examples.zh: 所有可用位置都放满后，我们测试了这个「有界栈」的表现。

collocations: test a bounded stack when full
push an item onto a bounded stack

words.enDefinition: A stack of changes or saved states used to undo the most recent change first.

examples.en: The editor added each change to the undo stack when we moved a shape on screen.
examples.zh: 我们在屏幕上移动图形时，编辑器把每次改动放进「撤销栈」。

examples.en: Our example read the undo stack to identify the last colour change made by the user.
examples.zh: 例题读取「撤销栈」，确定用户最近一次颜色改动。

collocations: push a change onto the undo stack
read the top of the undo stack

words.enDefinition: A stack of previously undone changes used to reapply the most recently undone change first.

examples.en: The practice editor put the undone colour change on the redo stack until we reapplied it.
examples.zh: 练习用的编辑器把已撤销的颜色改动放到「重做栈」中，等我们重新应用该改动。

examples.en: Our sample cleared the redo stack when the player made a different edit to the shape.
examples.zh: 玩家改用另一种方式编辑图形时，示例清空了「重做栈」。

collocations: push an undone change onto the redo stack
restore a change from the redo stack

words.enDefinition: A collection in which items are removed in the same order they were added.

examples.en: The printer example used a FIFO queue so earlier class projects were processed before later arrivals.
examples.zh: 打印示例采用「先进先出队列」，先处理较早到达的课堂项目。

examples.en: We drew a FIFO queue and numbered the cards in the order they left it.
examples.zh: 我们画了一个「先进先出队列」，按卡片离开队列的顺序给它们编号。

collocations: add work to a FIFO queue
process entries from a FIFO queue

words.enDefinition: Describing an order in which the first item added is the first removed.

examples.en: The ticket exercise used first-in, first-out order so earlier arrivals kept their places.
examples.zh: 取号练习采用「先进先出」顺序，让先到者保持原来的次序。

examples.en: Our tutor explained first in, first out by comparing card arrival times with card removal times.
examples.zh: 老师比较卡片的进入时间和取出时间来解释「先进先出」。

words.enDefinition: The first item in a queue, which is next to be removed in FIFO order.

examples.en: We marked the front element because it would leave the practice queue before the other cards.
examples.zh: 我们标出了「队首元素」，因为它会比其他卡片更早离开练习队列。

examples.en: The tutor displayed the front element without removing it from the small queue on screen.
examples.zh: 老师显示了「队首元素」，它仍留在屏幕上的小队列中。

collocations: inspect the front element without removing it

words.enDefinition: The item currently at the end where new items are added to a FIFO queue.

examples.en: The rear element changed when we put one more card into the practice queue.
examples.zh: 我们往练习用的队列再放入一张卡片后，「队尾元素」发生了变化。

examples.en: Our diagram placed the arrow for insertion directly after the current rear element in the queue.
examples.zh: 图中把入队箭头画在当前「队尾元素」的正后方。

collocations: add an item after the rear element

words.enDefinition: To insert an item at the end of a queue.

examples.en: The simulator would enqueue each colour card as soon as the student clicked its button.
examples.zh: 学生点击某张颜色卡的按钮后，模拟器马上让该卡「入队」。

examples.en: We watched the queue length increase after asking the program to enqueue two more items.
examples.zh: 让程序把另外两项「入队」后，我们看到队列变长了。

words.enDefinition: To remove the next item from the front of a queue, usually returning it.

examples.en: The program tried to dequeue a card each time the student clicked the next button.
examples.zh: 学生每次点击下一步按钮，程序都尝试让一张卡片「从队首出队」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked what value the queue would return if we chose to dequeue once.
examples.zh: 练习表问，如果执行一次「从队首出队」，队列会返回哪个值。

words.enDefinition: Trying to remove an item from a queue when it is empty.

examples.en: The exercise reported queue underflow after we tried to remove a card from an empty queue.
examples.zh: 我们尝试从空队列取出卡片后，练习报告了「队列下溢」。

examples.en: Our tutor drew an empty case to show the conditions that could cause queue underflow.
examples.zh: 老师画了一个空队列的例子，说明怎样会发生「队列下溢」。

collocations: handle queue underflow in a test

words.enDefinition: A queue with a fixed upper limit on the number of items it can hold.

examples.en: The bounded queue in our simulator could hold four samples and then had no space for more.
examples.zh: 模拟器中的「有界队列」最多放四个样本。

examples.en: We filled the bounded queue and checked how the exercise handled another arrival.
examples.zh: 我们填满了「有界队列」，然后查看练习怎样处理再到达的一项。

collocations: test a bounded queue at capacity

words.enDefinition: A queue with no fixed item limit in its interface, subject to available resources.

examples.en: The toy program used an unbounded queue with no fixed limit on waiting print jobs.
examples.zh: 示例程序采用「无界队列」，没有给等待打印的作业数量设固定上限。

examples.en: Our tutor explained that an unbounded queue still needed memory for every item stored.
examples.zh: 老师解释，「无界队列」仍需要占用内存来存放每一项。

collocations: use an unbounded queue for a demonstration
contrast an unbounded queue with a bounded queue

words.enDefinition: A FIFO queue in which array positions are reused as the front and rear indexes wrap around.

examples.en: We reused the first slot in our circular queue after earlier removals had made it available.
examples.zh: 先前几次出队腾出了位置，之后我们重新使用了「循环队列」的第一格。

examples.en: The worksheet traced a circular queue through several removals and additions using the same array.
examples.zh: 练习表用同一个数组演示「循环队列」的几次出队和入队。

collocations: represent a circular queue in an array

words.enDefinition: A fixed-capacity storage area that reuses positions in a cycle, often as part of a queue.

examples.en: The tiny sensor simulator used a ring buffer to retain the last few readings.
examples.zh: 小型传感器模拟器采用「环形缓冲区」保留最近的几个读数。

examples.en: Our diagram showed how a ring buffer could reuse the same five storage positions.
examples.zh: 图中展示了「环形缓冲区」怎样重复利用同样的五个存储位置。

collocations: write readings into a ring buffer

words.enDefinition: An indexing scheme that returns to the start of a storage area after reaching its end.

examples.en: The circular storage exercise used wrap-around indexing to return to position zero after the final slot.
examples.zh: 循环存储练习用「环绕索引」在到达最后一格后返回位置零。

examples.en: Our tutor labelled wrap-around indexing on the diagram showing both sides of the storage boundary.
examples.zh: 老师在图中跨越存储边界的位置标出了「环绕索引」。

collocations: illustrate wrap-around indexing in a ring buffer

words.enDefinition: In a buffer, the position from which the next unread item is taken.

examples.en: The read index pointed to the next sample that the toy buffer would return.
examples.zh: 「读取索引」指向示例缓冲区下一次要返回的样本。

examples.en: We moved the read index after taking one colour card from the buffer.
examples.zh: 从缓冲区取出一张颜色卡后，我们移动了「读取索引」。

words.enDefinition: In a buffer, the position where the next item is to be stored.

examples.en: The write index identified the location for the next reading in the sample buffer.
examples.zh: 「写入索引」标出了示例缓冲区中下一个读数要写入的位置。

examples.en: Our drawing showed the write index returning to the first slot after the last slot.
examples.zh: 图示显示，「写入索引」经过最后一格之后回到第一格。

words.enDefinition: A collection that supports adding and removing elements at both ends.

examples.en: The exercise used a deque so either end could accept a new playing card.
examples.zh: 练习采用「双端队列」，两端都可以放入新的扑克牌。

examples.en: Our tutor showed how a deque could act like a stack or a queue.
examples.zh: 老师演示了「双端队列」怎样既能当栈用，也能当队列用。

collocations: add an item to a deque
remove items from either end of a deque

words.enDefinition: To insert a new item at the front of a collection supporting that operation.

examples.en: The exercise let us push at the front so the new card became the first item.
examples.zh: 练习允许我们「在队列前端加入元素」，这样新卡片就成了第一项。

examples.en: Our tutor used a deque to show when we could push at the front.
examples.zh: 老师用双端队列演示什么时候可以「在队列前端加入元素」。

collocations: push at the front of a deque
push at the front of a container
choose when to push at the front

words.enDefinition: To remove the last item from a collection that permits removal at that end.

examples.en: The most recent card was at the back, so we chose to pop from the back.
examples.zh: 最后加入的卡片在队尾，所以我们选择「从队尾弹出元素」。

examples.en: We could pop from the back of the deque without moving any of the other items.
examples.zh: 我们可以从双端队列的「队尾弹出元素」，其他各项都无需移动。

collocations: pop from the back of a deque
pop from the back after checking the size
decide when to pop from the back

words.enDefinition: To shift the items cyclically so entries leaving one end reappear at the other.

examples.en: We could rotate a deque one step to bring the last card around to the front.
examples.zh: 我们可以把「双端队列旋转」一步，让最后一张卡片回到前端。

examples.en: The Python exercise asked us to rotate a deque without adding or removing any cards overall.
examples.zh: Python 练习要求我们「旋转双端队列」，保持卡片总数不变。

collocations: rotate a deque to the left
use a method to rotate a deque

words.enDefinition: the number of items currently stored in a queue

examples.en: The simulator displayed the queue length so we could see how many cards were waiting.
examples.zh: 模拟器显示「队列长度」，让我们看到有多少张卡片在等待。

examples.en: We compared the queue length before and after the printer accepted the next example job.
examples.zh: 我们对比了打印机接收下一项示例作业前后的「队列长度」。

words.enDefinition: A collection in which keys identify stored values instead of requiring sequential numeric positions.

examples.en: The example used an associative array to look up a colour's code by its name.
examples.zh: 例题用「关联数组」按颜色名称查找颜色代码。

examples.en: We stored each book title under its catalogue number in an associative array for the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，我们用「关联数组」，以各书的目录编号存放书名。

collocations: look up values in an associative array
store counts in an associative array

words.enDefinition: A key together with the value associated with it in a mapping.

examples.en: The sample program wrote one key-value pair for each name and score in the list.
examples.zh: 示例程序为列表里的每组姓名和分数写入一个「键值对」。

examples.en: We printed every key-value pair so the tutor could see which values belonged to which keys.
examples.zh: 我们输出每个「键值对」，方便老师看出各值对应哪个键。

words.enDefinition: An operation that searches a mapping for the value associated with a specified key.

examples.en: The example used a key lookup to retrieve the score for the requested player.
examples.zh: 示例通过「键查找」取得所查询玩家的分数。

examples.en: Our worksheet traced a key lookup for a book whose catalogue number was already stored.
examples.zh: 练习表跟踪了某本书的「键查找」过程，该书的目录编号早已存入。

words.enDefinition: A requested key for which the mapping contains no entry.

examples.en: The mapping returned the default score when the example asked for a missing key.
examples.zh: 例题查询一个「不存在的键」时，映射返回了默认分数。

examples.en: We tested a missing key using a colour name that the program had never stored.
examples.zh: 我们用程序从未存过的一种颜色名称测试了「不存在的键」。

collocations: return a default for a missing key

words.expression: default value for a missing key
words.lemma: default value for a missing key
words.enDefinition: A fallback value returned when a lookup does not find the requested key.
acceptedEnVariants: default value for a missing key

examples.en: The counting example used zero as the default value for a missing key in the dictionary.
examples.zh: 计数示例用零作为字典中「缺失键的默认值」。

examples.en: We supplied a default value for a missing key so the program could display a blank label.
examples.zh: 我们提供了一个「缺失键的默认值」，让程序可以显示空标签。

collocations: provide a default value for a missing key
choose a default value for a missing key
return a default value for a missing key

words.enDefinition: To change the value associated with an existing key in a mapping.

examples.en: Our code needed to update a mapping after the tutor corrected the score for one team.
examples.zh: 老师更正某一队的分数后，代码需要「更新映射中的值」。

examples.en: We asked the program to update a mapping while keeping the original key exactly as written.
examples.zh: 我们让程序在保留原键的同时「更新映射中的值」。

collocations: update a mapping for an existing key
update a mapping without changing its keys
decide when to update a mapping

words.enDefinition: To remove the association for a particular key so that the key is no longer present.

examples.en: The editor could delete a mapping when the selected colour was removed from the sample palette.
examples.zh: 从示例调色板移除选中的颜色时，编辑器可以「删除一条键值映射」。

examples.en: Our code checked that the key existed before trying to delete a mapping for that name.
examples.zh: 代码先核对该键是否存在，再尝试为这个名字「删除一条键值映射」。

collocations: delete a mapping for a removed entry
check the key before you delete a mapping

words.enDefinition: An object exposing the current keys of a mapping without making a separate copy of them.

examples.en: The dictionary's key view showed the new book number as soon as we added the entry.
examples.zh: 我们一加入条目，字典的「键视图」就显示了新的图书编号。

examples.en: We used the key view to read the stored names without copying them into a list.
examples.zh: 我们用「键视图」读出已存的姓名，无需把姓名复制到列表里。

collocations: check membership in a key view

words.enDefinition: An object exposing the current values in a mapping without copying them into a new collection.

examples.en: The values view included the same score twice because two different teams had earned it.
examples.zh: 由于两支队伍取得同样的分数，「值视图」中该分数出现了两次。

examples.en: Our exercise used the values view to total the recorded scores without examining any names.
examples.zh: 练习用「值视图」计算已记录的分数总和，无需查看姓名。

collocations: read values through a values view

words.enDefinition: An object exposing a mapping's current entries as key-value pairs without copying them.

examples.en: The dictionary's items view let us see each colour name beside its code in the example.
examples.zh: 例题中，字典的「键值对视图」让我们同时看到各颜色名称及其代码。

examples.en: We looked at the items view again after one value in the original dictionary changed.
examples.zh: 原字典的一项值变化后，我们又看了一次「键值对视图」。

collocations: inspect pairs in an items view

words.enDefinition: A data structure that stores distinct elements for membership checks and related operations.

examples.en: We put the selected colours in a set so duplicate choices counted only once.
examples.zh: 我们把选出的颜色放进「集合」，这样重复选择的颜色只计一次。

examples.en: The tutor asked how many elements a set would have after adding blue twice.
examples.zh: 老师问，两次添加蓝色后，「集合」里有多少元素。

collocations: add an element to a set
check whether a set contains an element

words.enDefinition: Source-code notation that directly creates a set from its specified elements.

examples.en: We wrote a nonempty set literal in Python to represent the three colours on the board.
examples.zh: 我们用 Python 写了一个非空「集合字面量」，表示板上的三种颜色。

examples.en: The example used a set literal containing repeated names, then printed the number of distinct entries.
examples.zh: 示例用了一个包含重复姓名的「集合字面量」，然后打印不同条目的数量。

collocations: initialize data with a set literal
use a set literal in an example

words.enDefinition: An operation checking whether a requested element belongs to a collection.

examples.en: The example used a membership test to check whether blue belonged to the allowed colour set.
examples.zh: 示例做了「成员测试」，检查蓝色是否属于允许使用的颜色集合。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a membership test on a set with scanning the original list of names.
examples.zh: 老师对比了在集合上做「成员测试」和逐项搜索原来的姓名列表。

collocations: a membership test on a set

words.enDefinition: A set containing every element present in either or both of the original sets.

examples.en: We used a set union to list every colour chosen by either team in the activity.
examples.zh: 我们用「集合的并集」列出活动中两队选过的所有颜色。

examples.en: Our diagram shaded both circles to show the complete set union for the two groups.
examples.zh: 图中把两个圆都涂上颜色，展示两组的整个「集合的并集」。

collocations: take the set union of two groups

words.enDefinition: A set containing only elements that belong to both of the original sets.

examples.en: The set intersection showed the colours that both teams selected during the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 「集合的交集」显示课堂练习中两队都选到的颜色。

examples.en: We checked whether the set intersection was empty after comparing the choices for both days.
examples.zh: 比较两天的选择之后，我们查看「集合的交集」是否为空。

collocations: take the set intersection of two groups

words.enDefinition: The elements in the first specified set that do not belong to the second set.

examples.en: We used a set difference to find colours chosen on Monday but not on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 我们用「集合的差集」找出周一选了、周二没选的颜色。

examples.en: The instructor reversed the two sets to show how the set difference could change.
examples.zh: 老师调换了两个集合的次序，展示「集合的差集」可能怎样变化。

collocations: check the order of operands in a set difference

words.enDefinition: The elements that belong to exactly one of two sets.

examples.en: The symmetric difference contained colours chosen by just one of the two teams in the game.
examples.zh: 「对称差集」包含游戏中仅有其中一队选过的颜色。

examples.en: We compared the symmetric difference with the union before colouring the worksheet's diagram.
examples.zh: 给练习表上的图涂色前，我们对照了「对称差集」和并集。

collocations: take the symmetric difference of two sets

words.enDefinition: A set contained in another set that has at least one additional element.

examples.en: The practice palette was a proper subset of the full palette because it lacked several colours.
examples.zh: 练习调色板是完整调色板的「真子集」，因为里面少了几种颜色。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why a set could never be a proper subset of itself.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么一个集合永远不能成为它自己的「真子集」。

collocations: draw a proper subset on a diagram

words.enDefinition: Sets that have no elements in common.

examples.en: The program recognised disjoint sets after finding no colours shared by the two palettes.
examples.zh: 程序发现两个调色板没有共同颜色，认定它们是「不相交的集合」。

examples.en: Our drawing used separate circles to represent disjoint sets of animals in the example.
examples.zh: 例题图示中，我们用彼此分开的圆表示两组「不相交的集合」。

words.enDefinition: To remove repeated occurrences of equal elements from a list.

examples.en: We needed to deduplicate a list before counting how many people had joined the game.
examples.zh: 在统计有多少人加入游戏之前，我们需要「对列表去重」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how to deduplicate a list while keeping each name's first occurrence in place.
examples.zh: 老师问，怎样「对列表去重」，同时保留各姓名第一次出现的顺序。

collocations: deduplicate a list while preserving order
use a set to deduplicate a list

words.enDefinition: A structure that uses a hash function to place and find entries by key.

examples.en: The classroom hash table stored paint colours so we could find them by name.
examples.zh: 课堂示例的「散列表」存放油漆颜色，方便按名称查找。

examples.en: Our diagram showed how the hash table found an entry after determining its bucket.
examples.zh: 图中展示了「散列表」在确定桶之后怎样找到条目。

collocations: insert entries into a hash table
look up a key in a hash table

words.enDefinition: A function that computes a hash code from a key to help locate entries in a table.

examples.en: The classroom hash function turned each colour name into a number for choosing a storage bucket.
examples.zh: 课堂示例的「散列函数」把每个颜色名变成一个数，用来选择存储桶。

examples.en: We applied the same hash function when adding an entry and when searching for it.
examples.zh: 我们在添加条目和查找条目时使用同一个「散列函数」。

collocations: apply a hash function to a key
compare the output of a hash function

words.enDefinition: The result produced by applying a hash function to an input.

examples.en: The example used the hash value to determine which storage bucket to check for the key.
examples.zh: 示例用「散列值」确定应在哪个存储桶里查找这个键。

examples.en: Two different inputs had the same hash value in the sample function shown on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 练习表中的样本函数对两个不同输入生成了相同的「散列值」。

collocations: derive a bucket from a hash value

words.enDefinition: A key with a stable hash during use and a hash consistent with how key equality is defined.

examples.en: The Python exercise used a tuple of integers as a hashable key for each square.
examples.zh: Python 练习中，每个格子都用一个整数元组作「可散列的键」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why an ordinary Python list could not be used as a hashable key.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么普通 Python 列表不能作为「可散列的键」。

words.enDefinition: The position identifying a bucket in the storage array of a hash table.

examples.en: The worksheet printed the bucket index next to the name assigned to that bucket.
examples.zh: 练习表把「桶索引」印在分配到该桶的姓名旁边。

examples.en: Our tutor recomputed the bucket index after changing the number of storage positions in the example.
examples.zh: 例题中存储位置数量变了，老师重新计算了「桶索引」。

collocations: map a hash value to a bucket index

words.enDefinition: an event where different keys produce the same hash value

examples.en: A hash collision occurred when the sample hash function produced the same value for two different colour names.
examples.zh: 示例散列函数为两个不同的颜色名生成同一个散列值，产生了「散列冲突」。

examples.en: The tutor illustrated a hash collision before showing how the table stored the two keys separately.
examples.zh: 在演示散列表如何分别存储两个键之前，导师先说明了一次「散列冲突」。

collocations: distinguish keys after a hash collision

words.enDefinition: a hash table technique that stores entries assigned to each bucket in an associated collection such as a linked list

examples.en: The classroom example used separate chaining to keep both colour entries together in one bucket.
examples.zh: 课堂示例用「链地址法」把两个颜色条目保存在同一个桶中。

examples.en: With separate chaining, we checked the entries in one bucket to find the matching name.
examples.zh: 使用「链地址法」时，我们核对同一个桶中的条目来找匹配名称。

collocations: implement a table with separate chaining

words.enDefinition: Resolving collisions by checking alternative positions within the table itself for insertion or lookup.

examples.en: The example used open addressing and looked for another slot when the first one was occupied.
examples.zh: 示例采用「开放寻址法」，第一个位置已被占用时就找另一个位置。

examples.en: Our tutor drew arrows across the array to explain how open addressing chose alternative positions.
examples.zh: 老师在数组上画出跨越各位置的箭头，说明「开放寻址法」怎样选备用位置。

collocations: find an empty slot with open addressing

words.enDefinition: The number of stored entries divided by the number of buckets or slots in a hash table.

examples.en: We calculated the load factor using six stored names and eight buckets in the example.
examples.zh: 例题中，我们用六个已存姓名和八个桶计算了「负载因子」。

examples.en: The load factor fell after the practice table gained more buckets without adding any entries.
examples.zh: 练习用的散列表增加了桶数，条目数维持原值，因此「负载因子」下降。

collocations: compare the load factor before and after resizing

words.enDefinition: To redistribute existing entries in a hash table by calculating their bucket positions again.

examples.en: We chose to rehash a table after adding more buckets in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 课堂示例增加桶数后，我们选择「对散列表重新散列」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked where the green entry would land when we needed to rehash a table.
examples.zh: 老师问，需要「对散列表重新散列」时，绿色条目会落在哪个位置。

collocations: rebuild buckets when you rehash a table
check the entries after you rehash a table

words.enDefinition: An object that tracks a traversal's current position and provides successive elements.

examples.en: The iterator returned one card at a time as we stepped through the example.
examples.zh: 我们逐步运行示例时，「迭代器」一次返回一张卡片。

examples.en: Our tutor created a second iterator so two students could read the cards independently.
examples.zh: 老师创建了第二个「迭代器」，让两名学生各自读取卡片。

words.enDefinition: an object that can supply an iterator so its values can be visited in order

examples.en: Our exercise accepted any iterable whose elements were numbers we could add together.
examples.zh: 练习接受任何元素都是可相加数值的「可迭代对象」。

examples.en: The tutor used a Python list as an iterable when demonstrating how iteration begins.
examples.zh: 老师演示遍历怎样开始时，用了一个 Python 列表作「可迭代对象」。

collocations: obtain an iterator from an iterable
pass an iterable to a function

words.enDefinition: The order in which a collection's elements are produced during traversal.

examples.en: The iteration order mattered because students compared the printed scores line by line with the example.
examples.zh: 学生要把输出的成绩逐行与示例核对，所以「迭代顺序」很重要。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the model guaranteed an iteration order for the set of colours.
examples.zh: 老师问，模型会不会保证这个颜色集合的「迭代顺序」。

words.enDefinition: The order in which distinct entries were originally added to a collection.

examples.en: The Python dictionary kept insertion order, so the names appeared in the sequence we added them.
examples.zh: Python 字典保留「插入顺序」，所以姓名按我们添加它们的次序出现。

examples.en: We chose to show the sample cards in insertion order instead of sorting them alphabetically.
examples.zh: 我们选择按「插入顺序」显示样本卡片，而非按字母顺序排序。

words.enDefinition: To visit a collection's elements in their iteration order.

examples.en: The exercise asked us to iterate over a collection of temperatures and print each reading.
examples.zh: 练习要求我们「遍历集合容器」里的温度值，并打印每个读数。

examples.en: Our tutor showed how to iterate over a collection before asking us to total its numeric values.
examples.zh: 老师先演示了怎样「遍历集合容器」，再让我们把里面的数值加总。

collocations: iterate over a collection of values
iterate over a collection without modifying it
use an iterator to iterate over a collection

words.enDefinition: To visit each mapping entry and obtain both its key and its associated value.

examples.en: We needed to iterate over entries because the table showed both each name and its score.
examples.zh: 表格既要显示姓名也要显示分数，因此我们需要「遍历映射条目」。

examples.en: The Python exercise used the dictionary's items method to iterate over entries as pairs.
examples.zh: Python 练习用字典的 items 方法「遍历映射条目」，逐个得到键值对。

collocations: iterate over entries in a map
iterate over entries to read each pair
iterate over entries without changing the keys

words.enDefinition: To move an iterator to the next position it can visit in a traversal.

examples.en: Our tutor asked what happened when we chose to advance an iterator beyond the final element.
examples.zh: 老师问，尝试把「迭代器推进」到最后一个元素之后时会发生什么。

examples.en: We needed to advance an iterator to reach the next card in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 为了到达课堂练习中的下一张卡片，我们需要「推进迭代器」。

collocations: advance an iterator by one position
advance an iterator to the next item
check the end before you advance an iterator

words.enDefinition: The state in which an iterator has no remaining values to produce.

examples.en: The Python example detected iterator exhaustion after it had returned every colour from the list.
examples.zh: Python 示例已经返回列表中的每种颜色后，检测到了「迭代器耗尽」。

examples.en: We created a new iterator after iterator exhaustion so we could read the sequence again.
examples.zh: 「迭代器耗尽」后，我们创建了一个新的迭代器，以便再次读取这个序列。

words.enDefinition: A change that prevents an existing iterator from being used reliably according to its collection's rules.

examples.en: Our C++ example showed iterator invalidation after a vector grew and moved to new storage.
examples.zh: C++ 示例展示了向量扩展并迁移到新存储位置后出现的「迭代器失效」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which changes caused iterator invalidation for the specific container used in the lab.
examples.zh: 老师问，对于实验课用的这个容器，哪些改动会导致「迭代器失效」。

collocations: check the container's rules for iterator invalidation

words.enDefinition: An iterator that visits elements in the reverse of a collection's usual iteration order.

examples.en: The example used a reverse iterator to display the newest saved measurements before the oldest.
examples.zh: 示例用「反向迭代器」先显示最新保存的测量值，再显示更早的值。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a reverse iterator with making a separate reversed copy of the card list.
examples.zh: 老师对比了使用「反向迭代器」与另建一份倒序卡片列表的做法。
